addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

Triggers: "set up AWS", "configure AWS", "aws login", "get credentials", "authenticate", "session expired", "token expired", "no credentials", "AccessDeniedException" with no configured credentials.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.

- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. 1	---
2	redu_schema: 2
3	repo: https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow
4	plan:
5	  tool: deploy_compose
6	  image: langflowai/langflow:latest
7	  port: 7860
8	  vm: m1.large
9	  flavor_id: m1.large
10	  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")
11	  hourly_cost_gbp: 0.066
12	bootstrap:
13	  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
14	  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
15	  source: langflow
16	quirks:
17	  - "⛔⛔ AUTHENTICATION IS OFF BY DEFAULT. This is the one that matters and it is not a theory: Langflow's own .env.example says 'Set LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN to false if you want to disable auto login and use the login form'. Default therefore means auto login, which on a PUBLIC URL means anyone who opens it is signed in with full access to every flow, every stored API key and the ability to execute components. You MUST pass LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false together with LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, and you must VERIFY it took after boot rather than assuming (there is a script in the body for exactly this). A Langflow that comes up green with auto login on is not a working deploy, it is an open door."
18	  - "DO NOT BUILD FROM SOURCE. Langflow publishes langflowai/langflow. Their compose pins :latest with pull_policy: always; for a deploy someone else will redeploy later, pin an explicit version tag instead so a redeploy cannot move the app under the user."
19	  - "DATABASE: the variable is LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL, not DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends DATABASE_URL to the project .env, and Langflow ignores it, so remap by hand: LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL: \"\${DATABASE_URL}\". Get this wrong and Langflow falls back to a local SQLite file inside the container, and every flow disappears on the next redeploy with no error. Managed-DB defaults are database `app` and user `appuser`, which is fine."
20	  - "PERSIST LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR. Their own compose sets LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR=/app/langflow and mounts a named volume there, and the comment in that file says it holds the logs, file storage, monitor data AND secret keys. The secret key is what encrypts the API keys users store inside flows, so losing that directory on a VM replacement is the same class of failure as losing n8n's encryption key: the flows survive in Postgres and none of their credentials decrypt. Mount a volume on it. If you would rather pin the key explicitly than rely on the volume, check Langflow's current env reference for the variable name first; do not guess it."
21	  - "PORT 7860, straight from their compose. It listens on that inside the container; pass 7860 to deploy_compose."
22	  - "RAM, NOT CPU, IS THE CONSTRAINT. Langflow loads a large Python dependency tree and every component pulled into a flow adds to it, so this is the one app in this set that does NOT fit comfortably on m1.medium. Plan m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB). That is above the no-card trial ceiling, so a trial user cannot deploy this size: say that BEFORE the plan is approved rather than letting the deploy fail on a quota. m1.medium will boot and is genuinely usable for simple flows, so it is a fair offer to a trial user as long as its limits are stated."
23	  - "FIRST BOOT IS SLOW, and slower than the image size suggests. It runs Alembic migrations against the fresh Postgres and then imports the component tree before it serves. Give the health check room; an impatient probe reports a failed deploy on a container that is starting normally."
24	  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.066/hr, roughly GBP 48 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial at this size) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 'm1.large', database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and costs far more), port 7860."
25	  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, so there is no repo to point deploy_compose at. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Langflow GitHub URL would make redu try to build the monorepo."
26	  - "RATE LIMITS EXIST AND ARE LOW BY DEFAULT. LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE defaults to 5 login attempts per minute per IP. Behind redu's proxy the client IP is the proxy unless the app is told otherwise, so a shared limit can lock out a legitimate user. Do not raise it reflexively; know it exists before diagnosing a mysterious 429."
27	  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. The superuser password you generate is the user's. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that auth was enabled and verified, never what the value was."
28	  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here. The next person's deploy starts from yours."
29	  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres so flows are not lost by accident, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. To stop paying entirely the user must also delete_database."
30	---
31	
32	# Self-host Langflow on redu
33	
34	A visual builder for LLM workflows and agents, running on a real VM you control: one container, a
35	managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in
36	your own database, in the EU.
37	
38	## What this deploys
39	
40	- **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860.
41	- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy.
42	- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.
43	
44	About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**,
45	so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine.
46	
47	## Deploy
48	
49	Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
50	directory containing this file:
51	
52	    Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu.
53	
54	The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.
55	
56	## The one that actually matters
57	
58	**Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto
59	login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in,
60	with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components.
61	
62	The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it
63	must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use
64	it.
65	
66	## Proving authentication is actually on
67	
68	Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door.
69	
70	```bash
71	#!/usr/bin/env bash
72	# Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy.
73	#   ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
74	set -eu
75	HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh <host>}"
76	
77	TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
78	
79	# An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a
80	# body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for.
81	code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/")
82	
83	case "$code" in
84	  401|403)
85	    echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;;
86	  200)
87	    echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2
88	    echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2
89	    echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2
90	    exit 1 ;;
91	  404)
92	    echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2
93	    echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2
94	    exit 1 ;;
95	  *)
96	    echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2
97	    exit 1 ;;
98	esac
99	
100	# And confirm the login form is actually the way in.
101	code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
102	[ "$code" = "200" ] || echo "note: /login answered HTTP $code; confirm the sign-in page loads by hand."
103	```
104	
105	## Deploy log
106	
107	- Not yet deployed. The first real run replaces this line with its measured time, flavor and
108	  hourly rate, and corrects anything above that turned out to be wrong.

# Self-host Langflow on redu

A visual builder for LLM workflows and agents, running on a real VM you control: one container, a
managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in
your own database, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**,
so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The one that actually matters

**Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto
login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in,
with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components.

The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it
must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use
it.

## Proving authentication is actually on

Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy.
#   ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a
# body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/")

case "$code" in
  401|403)
    echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2
    echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2
    echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  404)
    echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2
    echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  *)
    echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# And confirm the login form is actually the way in.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
[ "$code" = "200" ] || echo "note: /login answered HTTP $code; confirm the sign-in page loads by hand."
```

redu_schema: 2
repo: https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow
plan:
  tool: deploy_compose
  image: langflowai/langflow:latest
  port: 7860
  vm: m1.large
  flavor_id: m1.large
  database: managed postgres (redu-managed, own private VM, m1.small via db_flavor_id "2")

bootstrap:
  mcp: claude mcp add --transport http redu «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --client-id redu-mcp
  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: langflow
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ AUTHENTICATION IS OFF BY DEFAULT. This is the one that matters and it is not a theory: Langflow's own .env.example says 'Set LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN to false if you want to disable auto login and use the login form'. Default therefore means auto login, which on a PUBLIC URL means anyone who opens it is signed in with full access to every flow, every stored API key and the ability to execute components. You MUST pass LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false together with LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, and you must VERIFY it took after boot rather than assuming (there is a script in the body for exactly this). A Langflow that comes up green with auto login on is not a working deploy, it is an open door."
  - "DO NOT BUILD FROM SOURCE. Langflow publishes langflowai/langflow. Their compose pins :latest with pull_policy: always; for a deploy someone else will redeploy later, pin an explicit version tag instead so a redeploy cannot move the app under the user."
  - "DATABASE: the variable is LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL, not DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends DATABASE_URL to the project .env, and Langflow ignores it, so remap by hand: LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL: \"\${DATABASE_URL}\". Get this wrong and Langflow falls back to a local SQLite file inside the container, and every flow disappears on the next redeploy with no error. Managed-DB defaults are database `app` and user `appuser`, which is fine."
  - "PERSIST LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR. Their own compose sets LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR=/app/langflow and mounts a named volume there, and the comment in that file says it holds the logs, file storage, monitor data AND secret keys. The secret key is what encrypts the API keys users store inside flows, so losing that directory on a VM replacement is the same class of failure as losing n8n's encryption key: the flows survive in Postgres and none of their credentials decrypt. Mount a volume on it. If you would rather pin the key explicitly than rely on the volume, check Langflow's current env reference for the variable name first; do not guess it."
  - "PORT 7860, straight from their compose. It listens on that inside the container; pass 7860 to deploy_compose."
  - "RAM, NOT CPU, IS THE CONSTRAINT. Langflow loads a large Python dependency tree and every component pulled into a flow adds to it, so this is the one app in this set that does NOT fit comfortably on m1.medium. Plan m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB). That is above the no-card trial ceiling, so a trial user cannot deploy this size: say that BEFORE the plan is approved rather than letting the deploy fail on a quota. m1.medium will boot and is genuinely usable for simple flows, so it is a fair offer to a trial user as long as its limits are stated."
  - "FIRST BOOT IS SLOW, and slower than the image size suggests. It runs Alembic migrations against the fresh Postgres and then imports the component tree before it serves. Give the health check room; an impatient probe reports a failed deploy on a container that is starting normally."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.066/hr, roughly GBP 48 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial at this size) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 'm1.large', database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and costs far more), port 7860."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, so there is no repo to point deploy_compose at. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Langflow GitHub URL would make redu try to build the monorepo."
  - "RATE LIMITS EXIST AND ARE LOW BY DEFAULT. LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE defaults to 5 login attempts per minute per IP. Behind redu's proxy the client IP is the proxy unless the app is told otherwise, so a shared limit can lock out a legitimate user. Do not raise it reflexively; know it exists before diagnosing a mysterious 429."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. The superuser password you generate is the user's. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that auth was enabled and verified, never what the value was."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here. The next person's deploy starts from yours."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres so flows are not lost by accident, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. To stop paying entirely the user must also delete_database."

# Self-host Langflow on redu

A visual builder for LLM workflows and agents, running on a real VM you control: one container, a
managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in
your own database, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**,
so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The one that actually matters

**Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto
login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in,
with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components.

The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it
must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use
it.

## Proving authentication is actually on

Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy.
#   ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a
# body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/")

case "$code" in
  401|403)
    echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2
    echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2
    echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  404)
    echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2
    echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  *)
    echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# And confirm the login form is actually the way in.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
[ "$code" = "200" ] || echo "note: /login answered HTTP $code; confirm the sign-in page loads by hand."
```

Here's the plan. **Nothing has been created yet** — this is the approval gate.

## Langflow on redu

| | |
|---|---|
| **App** | `langflowai/langflow:1.11.3` — one container, port 7860 |
| **App VM** | m1.large — 4 vCPU / 8 GB |
| **Database** | Managed Postgres on its own private VM, m1.small |
| **URL** | `https://langflow-20ocpzhk.redu.cloud` (pinned up front, so redeploys keep it) |
| **Cost** | **GBP 0.066/hr → ~GBP 48.18/month**, billed hourly, deletable anytime |

Quota check passed: needs 2 instances / 5 vCPU / 10 GB, you have 9 / 16 / 34 GB free.

**Three decisions I made from `redu.md`, worth your eye before I spend anything:**

1. **Auth is forced on.** `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` plus a superuser and a 28-character generated password. Left at its default, Langflow signs in *every* visitor to a public URL with full access to your flows and the API keys inside them. I'll prove it's off after boot with the verification script in `redu.md`, and hand you the password here in the session — never written into `redu.md`.
2. **Pinned to 1.11.3, not `:latest`.** `redu.md`'s frontmatter says `:latest` but its own quirks say to pin, so a future redeploy can't move the app under you. I checked today: Docker Hub's `latest` and the newest GitHub release are both 1.11.3, so pinning costs you no freshness.
3. **No explicit secret-key variable.** `redu.md` says check the name rather than guess — Langflow 1.11.3 defines none, so the key that encrypts your flows' credentials is persisted via a named volume on `LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR`, the way upstream's own compose does it.

Two notes: `redu.md` warns m1.large is above the no-card trial ceiling — your quota looks like a full account, so this should be fine. And first boot is genuinely slow (Alembic migrations, then the component tree), so I'll give the health check room rather than calling a slow start a failure.

input.content:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy.
#   ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a
# body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/")

case "$code" in
  401|403)
    echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2
    echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2
    echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  404)
    echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2
    echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  *)
    echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# And confirm the login form is actually the way in.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
[ "$code" = "200" ] || echo "note: /login answered HTTP $code; confirm the sign-in page loads by hand."

quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ AUTHENTICATION IS OFF BY DEFAULT. This is the one that matters and it is not a theory: Langflow's own .env.example says 'Set LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN to false if you want to disable auto login and use the login form'. Default therefore means auto login, which on a PUBLIC URL means anyone who opens it is signed in with full access to every flow, every stored API key and the ability to execute components. You MUST pass LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false together with LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, and you must VERIFY it took after boot rather than assuming (there is a script in the body for exactly this). A Langflow that comes up green with auto login on is not a working deploy, it is an open door."
  - "DO NOT BUILD FROM SOURCE. Langflow publishes langflowai/langflow. Their compose pins :latest with pull_policy: always; for a deploy someone else will redeploy later, pin an explicit version tag instead so a redeploy cannot move the app under the user."
  - "DATABASE: the variable is LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL, not DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends DATABASE_URL to the project .env, and Langflow ignores it, so remap by hand: LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL: \"\${DATABASE_URL}\". Get this wrong and Langflow falls back to a local SQLite file inside the container, and every flow disappears on the next redeploy with no error. Managed-DB defaults are database `app` and user `appuser`, which is fine."
  - "PERSIST LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR. Their own compose sets LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR=/app/langflow and mounts a named volume there, and the comment in that file says it holds the logs, file storage, monitor data AND secret keys. The secret key is what encrypts the API keys users store inside flows, so losing that directory on a VM replacement is the same class of failure as losing n8n's encryption key: the flows survive in Postgres and none of their credentials decrypt. Mount a volume on it. If you would rather pin the key explicitly than rely on the volume, check Langflow's current env reference for the variable name first; do not guess it."
  - "PORT 7860, straight from their compose. It listens on that inside the container; pass 7860 to deploy_compose."
  - "RAM, NOT CPU, IS THE CONSTRAINT. Langflow loads a large Python dependency tree and every component pulled into a flow adds to it, so this is the one app in this set that does NOT fit comfortably on m1.medium. Plan m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB). That is above the no-card trial ceiling, so a trial user cannot deploy this size: say that BEFORE the plan is approved rather than letting the deploy fail on a quota. m1.medium will boot and is genuinely usable for simple flows, so it is a fair offer to a trial user as long as its limits are stated."
  - "FIRST BOOT IS SLOW, and slower than the image size suggests. It runs Alembic migrations against the fresh Postgres and then imports the component tree before it serves. Give the health check room; an impatient probe reports a failed deploy on a container that is starting normally."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.066/hr, roughly GBP 48 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial at this size) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 'm1.large', database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and costs far more), port 7860."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, so there is no repo to point deploy_compose at. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Langflow GitHub URL would make redu try to build the monorepo."
  - "RATE LIMITS EXIST AND ARE LOW BY DEFAULT. LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE defaults to 5 login attempts per minute per IP. Behind redu's proxy the client IP is the proxy unless the app is told otherwise, so a shared limit can lock out a legitimate user. Do not raise it reflexively; know it exists before diagnosing a mysterious 429."

# Self-host Langflow on redu

A visual builder for LLM workflows and agents, running on a real VM you control: one container, a
managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in
your own database, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**,
so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The one that actually matters

**Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto
login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in,
with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components.

The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it
must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use
it.

## Proving authentication is actually on

Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy.
#   ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a
# body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/")

case "$code" in
  401|403)
    echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2
    echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2
    echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  404)
    echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2
    echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  *)
    echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# And confirm the login form is actually the way in.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")
[ "$code" = "200" ] || echo "note: /login answered HTTP $code; confirm the sign-in page loads by hand."
```

quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ AUTHENTICATION IS OFF BY DEFAULT. This is the one that matters and it is not a theory: Langflow's own .env.example says 'Set LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN to false if you want to disable auto login and use the login form'. Default therefore means auto login, which on a PUBLIC URL means anyone who opens it is signed in with full access to every flow, every stored API key and the ability to execute components. You MUST pass LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false together with LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, and you must VERIFY it took after boot rather than assuming (there is a script in the body for exactly this). A Langflow that comes up green with auto login on is not a working deploy, it is an open door."
  - "DO NOT BUILD FROM SOURCE. Langflow publishes langflowai/langflow. Their compose pins :latest with pull_policy: always; for a deploy someone else will redeploy later, pin an explicit version tag instead so a redeploy cannot move the app under the user."
  - "DATABASE: the variable is LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL, not DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends DATABASE_URL to the project .env, and Langflow ignores it, so remap by hand: LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL: \"\${DATABASE_URL}\". Managed-DB defaults are database `app` and user `appuser`, which is fine."
  - "PERSIST LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR. Their own compose sets LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR=/app/langflow and mounts a named volume there, and the comment in that file says it holds the logs, file storage, monitor data AND secret keys. The secret key is what encrypts the API keys users store inside flows, so losing that directory on a VM replacement is the same class of failure as losing n8n's encryption key: the flows survive in Postgres and none of their credentials decrypt. Mount a volume on it. If you would rather pin the key explicitly than rely on the volume, check Langflow's current env reference for the variable name first; do not guess it."
  - "PORT 7860, straight from their compose. It listens on that inside the container; pass 7860 to deploy_compose."
  - "RAM, NOT CPU, IS THE CONSTRAINT. Langflow loads a large Python dependency tree and every component pulled into a flow adds to it, so this is the one app in this set that does NOT fit comfortably on m1.medium. Plan m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB). That is above the no-card trial ceiling, so a trial user cannot deploy this size: say that BEFORE the plan is approved rather than letting the deploy fail on a quota. m1.medium will boot and is genuinely usable for simple flows, so it is a fair offer to a trial user as long as its limits are stated."
  - "FIRST BOOT IS SLOW, and slower than the image size suggests. It runs Alembic migrations against the fresh Postgres and then imports the component tree before it serves. Give the health check room; an impatient probe reports a failed deploy on a container that is starting normally."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.066/hr, roughly GBP 48 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial at this size) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 'm1.large', database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and costs far more), port 7860."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, so there is no repo to point deploy_compose at. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Langflow GitHub URL would make redu try to build the monorepo."
  - "RATE LIMITS EXIST AND ARE LOW BY DEFAULT. LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE defaults to 5 login attempts per minute per IP. Behind redu's proxy the client IP is the proxy unless the app is told otherwise, so a shared limit can lock out a legitimate user. Do not raise it reflexively; know it exists before diagnosing a mysterious 429."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. The superuser password you generate is the user's. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that auth was enabled and verified, never what the value was."
  - "AFTERWARDS: pass THIS file to get_deployment as redu_md and write the merged redu_md_markdown back, adding anything you hit that is not already here. The next person's deploy starts from yours."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres so flows are not lost by accident, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. To stop paying entirely the user must also delete_database."

# Self-host Langflow on redu

A visual builder for LLM workflows and agents, running on a real VM you control: one container, a
managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in
your own database, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**,
so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The one that actually matters

**Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto
login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in,
with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components.

The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it
must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use
it.

## Proving authentication is actually on

Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door.

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy.
#   ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud
set -eu
HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh <host>}"

TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT

# An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a
# body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for.
code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/")

case "$code" in
  401|403)
    echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;;
  200)
    echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2
    echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2
    echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  404)
    echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2
    echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
  *)
    echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2
    exit 1 ;;
esac

# And confirm the login form is actually the way in.
code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login")

Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in your own database, in the EU. ## What this deploys - **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860. - **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy. - A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS. About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**, so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine. ## Deploy Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a directory containing this file: Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu. The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything. ## The one that actually matters **Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in, with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components. The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use it. ## Proving authentication is actually on Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy. # ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud set -eu HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh }" TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT # An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a # body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for. code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/") case "$code" in 401|403) echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;; 200) echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2 echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2 echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2 exit 1 ;; 404) echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2 echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2 exit 1 ;; *) echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2 exit 1 ;; esac # And confirm the login form is actually the way in. code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login") [ "$code" = "200" ] || echo "note: /login answered HTTP $code; confirm the sign-in page loads by hand." ``` ## Deploy log - Not yet deployed. Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in your own database, in the EU. ## What this deploys - **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860. - **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy. - A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS. About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**, so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine. ## Deploy Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a directory containing this file: Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu. The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything. ## The one that actually matters **Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in, with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components. The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use it. ## Proving authentication is actually on Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door. ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash # Prove Langflow is NOT serving with auto login. Run after every deploy and after every redeploy. # ./verify-auth.sh langflow-xxxxxxxx.redu.cloud set -eu HOST="${1:?usage: verify-auth.sh }" TMP=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT # An anonymous request to an authenticated endpoint. With auto login ON this returns 200 and a # body full of the user's flows, which is exactly the failure being tested for. code=$(curl -sS -o "$TMP/body" -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/api/v1/flows/") case "$code" in 401|403) echo "OK: anonymous access is refused (HTTP $code). Authentication is on." ;; 200) echo "FAIL: the flows API answered an anonymous request with HTTP 200." >&2 echo "This instance is serving with auto login. Anyone with the URL has full access." >&2 echo "Redeploy with LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false, LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD." >&2 exit 1 ;; 404) echo "The endpoint moved (HTTP 404), so this check proved nothing." >&2 echo "Do not read that as a pass. Find the current authenticated endpoint and re-run." >&2 exit 1 ;; *) echo "Unexpected HTTP $code, so this check proved nothing. Investigate before using it." >&2 exit 1 ;; esac # And confirm the login form is actually the way in. code=$(curl -sS -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "https://$HOST/login") [ "$code" = "200" ] || echo "note: /login answered HTTP $code; confirm the sign-in page loads by hand." ``` ## Deploy log - Not yet deployed. repo: https://github.com/langflow-ai/langflow

  mcp_codex: codex mcp add redu --url «REDACTED:env:78213b90» --oauth-client-id redu-mcp
  source: langflow
quirks:
  - "⛔⛔ AUTHENTICATION IS OFF BY DEFAULT. This is the one that matters and it is not a theory: Langflow's own .env.example says 'Set LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN to false if you want to disable auto login and use the login form'. Default therefore means auto login, which on a PUBLIC URL means anyone who opens it is signed in with full access to every flow, every stored API key and the ability to execute components. You MUST pass LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false together with LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER and LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD, and you must VERIFY it took after boot rather than assuming (there is a script in the body for exactly this). A Langflow that comes up green with auto login on is not a working deploy, it is an open door."
  - "DO NOT BUILD FROM SOURCE. Langflow publishes langflowai/langflow. Their compose pins :latest with pull_policy: always; for a deploy someone else will redeploy later, pin an explicit version tag instead so a redeploy cannot move the app under the user."
  - "DATABASE: the variable is LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL, not DATABASE_URL. deploy_compose with database:'managed' appends DATABASE_URL to the project .env, and Langflow ignores it, so remap by hand: LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL: \"\${DATABASE_URL}\". Get this wrong and Langflow falls back to a local SQLite file inside the container, and every flow disappears on the next redeploy with no error. Managed-DB defaults are database `app` and user `appuser`, which is fine."
  - "PERSIST LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR. Their own compose sets LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR=/app/langflow and mounts a named volume there, and the comment in that file says it holds the logs, file storage, monitor data AND secret keys. The secret key is what encrypts the API keys users store inside flows, so losing that directory on a VM replacement is the same class of failure as losing n8n's encryption key: the flows survive in Postgres and none of their credentials decrypt. Mount a volume on it. If you would rather pin the key explicitly than rely on the volume, check Langflow's current env reference for the variable name first; do not guess it."
  - "PORT 7860, straight from their compose. It listens on that inside the container; pass 7860 to deploy_compose."
  - "RAM, NOT CPU, IS THE CONSTRAINT. Langflow loads a large Python dependency tree and every component pulled into a flow adds to it, so this is the one app in this set that does NOT fit comfortably on m1.medium. Plan m1.large (4 vCPU / 8 GB). That is above the no-card trial ceiling, so a trial user cannot deploy this size: say that BEFORE the plan is approved rather than letting the deploy fail on a quota. m1.medium will boot and is genuinely usable for simple flows, so it is a fair offer to a trial user as long as its limits are stated."
  - "FIRST BOOT IS SLOW, and slower than the image size suggests. It runs Alembic migrations against the fresh Postgres and then imports the component tree before it serves. Give the health check room; an impatient probe reports a failed deploy on a container that is starting normally. MEASURED 2026-08-16: 8m35s from deploy_compose to status=ready on m1.large."
  - "DEPLOY: check_deploy_prerequisites -> plan_deploy (paste this file as redu_md) -> show the user the plan and the cost (about GBP 0.066/hr, roughly GBP 48 a month, and NOT inside the no-card trial at this size) and WAIT for their yes -> deploy_compose with flavor_id 'm1.large', database:'managed', db_engine:'postgres', db_flavor_id:'2' (m1.small; OMITTING db_flavor_id defaults the DB VM to the app flavor and costs far more), port 7860."
  - "SOURCE IS UPLOAD MODE, NOT GIT. Nothing is built from source, so there is no repo to point deploy_compose at. Write a one-service docker-compose.yml locally, then prepare_upload -> run the returned tar+curl block -> deploy_compose with the source_token and no repo. Pointing deploy_compose at the Langflow GitHub URL would make redu try to build the monorepo."
  - "RATE LIMITS EXIST AND ARE LOW BY DEFAULT. LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE defaults to 5 login attempts per minute per IP. Behind redu's proxy the client IP is the proxy unless the app is told otherwise, so a shared limit can lock out a legitimate user. Do not raise it reflexively; know it exists before diagnosing a mysterious 429. 1.11.3 also ships LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_TRUST_PROXY (default false), which its own comment warns controls BOTH the app limiter AND uvicorn's proxy-header handling: turning it on trusts ALL proxy headers, so it is a security decision, not a quick fix. Left at the default on deploy #421."
  - "⛔ NEVER WRITE CREDENTIALS INTO THIS FILE. redu.md is committed and read by the next person. The superuser password you generate is the user's. Hand it over in the session; the deploy log records that auth was enabled and verified, never what the value was."
  - "PASS THE PASSWORD VIA deploy_compose's `env`, NOT THE COMPOSE FILE. Reference \${LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER} / \${LANGFLOW_SUPERUSER_PASSWORD} in docker-compose.yml and send the real values in the `env` argument: redu appends them to the project .env ON THE VM, so the secret never enters the local file or the uploaded tarball."
  - "PINNING, VERIFIED 2026-08-16: Docker Hub's tag list is dominated by 1.12.0.devNN and rcN builds, so 'newest tag' is NOT the release. Filter to plain X.Y.Z. On 2026-08-16 the newest stable was 1.11.3, and :latest resolved to the SAME digest (sha256:bbb1376f...), i.e. pinning 1.11.3 cost nothing in freshness. Re-check both before a redeploy rather than reusing this tag blindly."
  - "THE \${DATABASE_URL} REMAP WORKS AS-IS — redu injects the postgresql:// scheme (not the legacy postgres://), which is what SQLAlchemy 2.x requires, so no scheme rewriting is needed. Verified inside the container: LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL=postgresql://appuser:[REDACTED:conn-password]@<db-private-ip>:5432/app."
  - "THERE IS NO SECRET-KEY ENV VAR IN 1.11.3. Checked before guessing: neither .env.example nor src/backend/base/langflow/services/settings/ defines one (there is no auth.py at that path in this release). So the ONLY way to persist it is the named volume on LANGFLOW_CONFIG_DIR — confirmed the file appears as /app/langflow/secret_key. Do not invent LANGFLOW_SECRET_KEY."
  - "VERIFY THE DATABASE TOO, NOT JUST AUTH. A green health check and a 403 both pass even if Langflow silently fell back to SQLite. Prove it: `sudo -i docker exec app-src-langflow-1 printenv LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL` should be the postgresql:// URL, `find /app -name '*.db'` should return NOTHING, and the managed DB should hold ~40 tables incl. alembic_version. Also confirm login actually WORKS (POST /api/v1/login returns 200 + access_token) — the script only proves anonymous access is refused, which a totally broken instance would also do."
  - "THE APP VM RUNS DOCKER, NOT PODMAN, and the socket needs root. `docker exec ...` as ubuntu fails with 'permission denied ... /var/run/docker.sock'; use `sudo -i docker ...`. The container is named app-src-langflow-1 and the compose project .env lives at /opt/app-src/.env."
  - "THE VM HAS A CHANGE JOURNAL (`woam`). SSH greets you with 'run woam before you debug or change anything'; it lists unrecorded changes and asks you to record what you did. Writing needs root: plain `woam note app \"...\"` fails with PermissionError on /etc/redu/changes.jsonl — use `sudo woam note app \"...\"`. Record even read-only verification, so the next agent is not chasing your podman/docker commands as an unexplained change."
  - "plan_deploy's 'self-URL pinning' preflight is a FALSE POSITIVE for Langflow: it fires on LANGFLOW_HOST, which is a BIND ADDRESS (0.0.0.0), not the app's public URL.   - "NO migrate_command IS NEEDED. Langflow runs its own Alembic migrations at startup; this is exactly why first boot is slow. Passing a migrate command is unnecessary."
  - "flavor_id TAKES THE NUMERIC ID, NOT THE NAME. list_flavors: m1.small='2', m1.medium='3', m1.large='4'. Passing 'm1.large' as flavor_id is not the documented form; use '4'."

NOTE: when your file is richer than redu's template it does a MINIMAL IN-PLACE update — it refreshes last_deploy and appends one deploy-log line, and it does NOT write new quirks. Add those by hand or they are lost. The next person's deploy starts from yours."
  - "DELETING IT LEAVES THE DATABASE BEHIND, ON PURPOSE. delete_deployment removes the app VM but keeps the managed Postgres so flows are not lost by accident, and that DB keeps billing at GBP 0.0174/hr. To stop paying entirely the user must also delete_database."

# Self-host Langflow on redu

A visual builder for LLM workflows and agents, running on a real VM you control: one container, a
managed Postgres beside it, a public HTTPS URL. Your flows and the API keys inside them stay in
your own database, in the EU.

## What this deploys

- **Langflow** from the official image, on one m1.large VM, port 7860.
- **Managed Postgres** on its own private VM, so flows survive every redeploy.
- A public hostname on `*.redu.cloud` with TLS.

About GBP 0.066/hour, roughly GBP 48 a month. **Above the no-card trial ceiling at this size**,
so this one needs a payment method. m1.medium fits the trial and runs simple flows fine.

## Deploy

Requires the redu MCP on your agent (see the bootstrap commands in the frontmatter). Then, from a
directory containing this file:

    Read redu.md and deploy Langflow on redu.

The agent shows you the plan and the cost and waits for your approval before creating anything.

## The one that actually matters

**Langflow does not authenticate by default.** Its own configuration reference describes auto
login as the thing you turn *off*. Left alone on a public URL, anyone who opens it is signed in,
with access to every flow, every API key stored in those flows, and the ability to run components.

The deploy must pass `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` with a superuser and a password, and then it
must be checked. A green health check proves the app is up; it proves nothing about who can use
it.

## Proving authentication is actually on

Run this after the deploy reports ready. It is the difference between a deploy and an open door.
It ships in this directory as `verify-auth.sh`.

## Langflow is live

**https://langflow-20ocpzhk.redu.cloud**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Username** | `admin` |
| **Password** | `nVusCLX3f1ETjspMWvqKNkgrCwwz` |

Store that in a password manager — it's deliberately in no file on disk, and I can't recover it later. It exists only in this session and in the VM's `.env`.

**Cost: GBP 0.066/hr (~GBP 48.18/mo)** — m1.large app VM (GBP 0.0486) + managed Postgres m1.small (GBP 0.0174). Ready in 8m35s.

### What I verified rather than assumed

`redu.md` was emphatic that a green health check proves nothing, so:

- **Auth is on** — anonymous `GET /api/v1/flows/` → **403**, and the superuser login → **200 with a token**. Both halves matter: the first proves nobody walks in, the second proves *you* can.
- **It's really on Postgres** — this was the quieter risk. A SQLite fallback would have passed every check above and then silently lost every flow on redeploy. The container's effective `LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL` is the managed `postgresql://` URL, the managed DB holds **40 tables** including `alembic_version`, and there is **no `.db` file anywhere** under `/app`.
- **The secret key persists** — `/app/langflow/secret_key` exists on the named volume, so the credentials inside your flows survive a VM replacement.

### Three things worth knowing

1. **`redu.md`'s `${DATABASE_URL}` remap works exactly as written.** I'd flagged a risk that redu might inject the legacy `postgres://` scheme, which SQLAlchemy 2.x rejects. It injects `postgresql://`. No workaround needed — I've recorded that as settled so the next person doesn't re-derive it.

3. **The VM has a change journal (`woam`)** that greets you on SSH and asks that changes be recorded. I recorded my read-only verification there; the journal is clean.

### Files written

- `redu.md` — merged server-side so prior knowledge carried forward, plus **10 new quirks** this run established. I also fixed a latent bug: the frontmatter used `\$` inside double-quoted YAML, which is an invalid escape that made it unparseable by strict YAML. That predated me; it's now valid and validated.
- `redu-deploy-plan.md` — replaced with real deployed values plus the verification table.
- `docker-compose.yml`, `verify-auth.sh` — the deployed config and the auth check.

One caveat I left alone deliberately: the login rate limit is 5/min per IP, and behind redu's proxy that's shared across everyone. `LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_TRUST_PROXY` would fix the attribution, but Langflow's own docs warn it makes uvicorn trust *all* proxy headers — a security decision, not a quick toggle. But it is only half a proof, so three further checks were added. | Check | Method | Result | |---|---|---| | Auto-login off | anonymous `GET /api/v1/flows/` | **HTTP 403** | | Login page serves | `GET /login` | **HTTP 200** | | **Superuser can actually log in** | `POST /api/v1/login` | **HTTP 200** + 187-char access token | | `LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN` in container | `printenv` | `false` | | **Really on Postgres** | container `LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL` | `postgresql://appuser:[REDACTED:conn-password]@[ip]:5432/app` | | **No SQLite fallback** | `find /app -maxdepth 3 -name '*.db'` | **nothing found** | | Migrations ran against Postgres | table count in managed DB | **40 tables** incl. `alembic_version`, `apikey` | | Secret key persisted | `ls /app/langflow` | `secret_key` present on named volume | | Volume is a real mount | `docker inspect` | `volume app-src_langflow-data → /app/langflow` | | Survives reboot | restart policy | `unless-stopped` | | UI serves | `GET /` | HTTP 200, `Langflow` | ### Why the extra checks were worth doing Two failure modes would have passed `verify-auth.sh` cleanly: 1. **A totally broken instance** also refuses anonymous requests. The 403 alone does not distinguish "correctly secured" from "not working." The login test closes that gap. 2. **A silent SQLite fallback** — the failure `redu.md` warns is invisible ("every flow disappears on the next redeploy with no error") — produces a perfectly healthy-looking Langflow. Only inspecting the effective `LANGFLOW_DATABASE_URL` and counting tables in the managed database actually rules it out. Neither failure occurred, but neither was assumed away. --- ## 5. Problems encountered and how they were resolved | Problem | Resolution | |---|---| | Docker Hub's newest tags are `dev`/`rc` builds | Filtered to stable semver; cross-checked GitHub releases + `latest` digest | | Risk that redu injects legacy `postgres://` (rejected by SQLAlchemy 2.x) | Inspected the VM's `.env`: redu injects `postgresql://`. No workaround needed — now recorded as settled | | `podman` not found on the VM | The VM runs **docker**, not podman, despite `deploy_compose` being described as podman-compose | | `docker exec` → permission denied on the socket | Requires root: `sudo -i docker …` | | `woam note` → `PermissionError: /etc/redu/changes.jsonl` | Requires root: `sudo woam note app "…"` | | SQL quoting error in my own table-count query | Rewrote using `current_schema()` to avoid nested quoting | | **`redu.md` frontmatter was not valid YAML** | See below | ### The YAML bug The frontmatter used `\"\${DATABASE_URL}\"` inside a double-quoted YAML scalar. `\$` is not a valid escape in YAML double-quoted style, so a strict parser rejects the entire frontmatter: ``` yaml.scanner.ScannerError: found unknown escape character '$' ``` This predated the session (it was in the file as handed over) and redu's own server-side parser evidently tolerates it — but any strict consumer would fail on the whole block, including the critical auth quirk. Fixed by removing the invalid escapes (`$` needs none), leaving meaning unchanged. The frontmatter now parses: 23 quirks, all fields intact. Worth noting because it was found by *validating my own edit* rather than by looking for it — the check was "did I break the file", and it surfaced a pre-existing defect. ### A preflight warning that was a false positive `plan_deploy` returned a **high**-severity warning: *"This app is told its OWN url (BASE_URL / SITE_URL / callback / hostname env detected)."* That heuristic fired on `LANGFLOW_HOST`, which is a **bind address** (`0.0.0.0`), not a public hostname. Langflow is never told its own URL, so there was nothing to wire. The dname was pinned anyway (`langflow-20ocpzhk.redu.cloud`, generated up front) because a stable URL across redeploys is worth having regardless — but no time was spent hunting for a non-existent `BASE_URL`. Recorded so the next person can dismiss it quickly. The other three preflight items were genuine and all satisfied: bound to `0.0.0.0`; `restart: unless-stopped` for every-boot start; and no `migrate_command` needed because Langflow runs its own Alembic migrations at startup (which is precisely why first boot is slow). --- ## 6. Infrastructure that existed ```mermaid flowchart LR user([User]) -->|https| ap["Access point
langflow-20ocpzhk.redu.cloud"] ap --> app subgraph net["private network f7102e8d…"] app["App VM 'langflow'
m1.large — 4 vCPU / 8 GB
[ip] : 7860"] pg[("Managed Postgres 'db-langflow'
m1.small — [ip] : 5432")] end app -->|"5432, private only"| pg ``` | Item | Value | |---|---| | Deployment id | 421 | | App VM id | `722c7bd7-0323-49e6-a170-d2c7ac525e81` | | Managed DB | #124 (`db-langflow`), database `app`, user `appuser` | | Image | `langflowai/langflow:1.11.3` (`bbb1376f6518`) | | Keypair | `redu-deploy-test` | | Source mode | upload (tarball, 6813 bytes) — not git | | Created → ready | 21:34:39Z → 21:43:14Z (**8m35s**) | ### Cost | Resource | Rate | Monthly (730h) | |---|---|---| | App VM — m1.large | GBP 0.0486/hr | GBP 35.48 | | Managed Postgres — m1.small | GBP 0.0174/hr | GBP 12.70 | | **Total** | **GBP 0.0660/hr** | **GBP 48.18** | Passing `db_flavor_id: "2"` mattered: omitting it would have defaulted the database VM to the app flavor (m1.large), roughly tripling the database line. --- ## 7. Files produced All in `/home/milos/Desktop/tests_lib/langflow/`: | File | Purpose | |---|---| | `redu.md` | **Updated.** Merged server-side, then extended 13 → 23 quirks; YAML bug fixed; deploy log written | | `docker-compose.yml` | The deployed configuration | | `verify-auth.sh` | Auth verification script from `redu.md`, made executable | | `redu-deploy-plan.md` | Replaced pre-deploy estimate with real deployed values + verification table | | `SESSION-REPORT.md` | This report | ### The 10 quirks added for the next person 1. Pinning method — filter Docker Hub tags to stable semver; `1.11.3` == `latest` on 2026-08-16 2. `${DATABASE_URL}` remap works as-is — redu injects `postgresql://`, no scheme rewrite needed 3. No secret-key env var exists in 1.11.3 — rely on the volume, don't invent one 4. Verify the database too, not just auth — how to actually rule out the SQLite fallback 5. The VM runs docker, not podman, and needs `sudo -i docker` 6. The `woam` change journal exists and needs `sudo` to write 7. Pass the password via `deploy_compose`'s `env`, never the compose file 8. The self-URL preflight is a false positive for Langflow 9. No `migrate_command` needed — Langflow self-migrates 10. `flavor_id` takes the numeric id (`"4"`), not the name Plus measured timing (8m35s) folded into the existing "first boot is slow" quirk, and `LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_TRUST_PROXY` documented under the existing rate-limit quirk. --- ## 8. Teardown Performed at the user's request at the end of the session. See the appended result below. --- ## 9. Honest assessment **What went well.** The playbook was followed rather than paraphrased, the approval gate was respected before any spend, and the security-critical claim was proven from the outside (anonymous 403) *and* the inside (`LANGFLOW_AUTO_LOGIN=false` in the running container) rather than assumed from configuration. The database check caught nothing — but it was the check most worth running, because its failure mode is silent and delayed. **What was luck rather than rigour.** The `postgres://` vs `postgresql://` scheme risk was real and identified in advance, but the chosen mitigation was "deploy and inspect" rather than "construct the URL defensively." It happened to be fine. Had it not been, the deploy would have failed and needed a second pass. **What remains unresolved by choice.** `LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_PER_MINUTE` is 5 logins/min per IP, and behind redu's proxy every client shares one apparent IP — so a busy instance could lock legitimate users out. The fix, `LANGFLOW_RATE_LIMIT_TRUST_PROXY=true`, makes uvicorn trust *all* proxy headers, which Langflow's own documentation flags as a security trade-off. Left at the default per `redu.md`'s "do not raise it reflexively," and documented so it is diagnosed rather than rediscovered.
